sections.html:
Parker sits in the northeast corner of Douglas County, about 23 miles southeast of downtown Denver. Castle Rock, where the county offices are, lies roughly 15 miles southwest. Aurora shares Parker's northeastern boundary. Population was 58,512 in the 2020 census, and the 2024 estimate is 65,473.

Homes here are scarce. Of 21,443 housing units in 2020, only 3.1% stood empty, and the homeowner vacancy rate was 0.8%. With a median household income of $120,075 in the 2022 survey, a typical Parker buyer is financing and expects the house to pass a lender's appraisal. A well-kept home meets that bar without trouble. A property with postponed repairs, a tenant who is hard to work with or an unsettled estate has a rougher time in front of those buyers.

sections.h2: Why many Parker houses are reaching repair age
sections.html:
Most of Parker was built in two surges, one in the mid-1990s and another in the mid-2000s, while Denver's southern suburbs kept spreading. As a result, plenty of houses are now about 20 to 30 years old. Roofs, water heaters and the appliances that came with the house tend to fail around that age, and an inspector hired by the buyer will list every one of them.

An owner in that spot has three options. Pay for the work before listing. Offer the buyer a credit and live with a lower price. Or find a buyer who takes the house as it stands and plans the repairs afterward. The right pick depends on how much cash you can spare and how soon you must move.

Before choosing, walk the house with a notebook. Note the age of the roof and water heater, any appliance that is original to the house, and every spot where water has ever shown up. A written list gives you a firm basis for comparing a credit against a repair, and it keeps a buyer's inspection from turning into a negotiation about things you never saw.

sections.h2: Flood checks, basements and school boundaries
sections.html:
Cherry Creek winds through Parker, and a few gulches run toward it. Own a house near either one? Look up the floodplain status before you list, and jot down anything you remember about water in a basement. Insurers and buyers raise the subject sooner or later, and a plain answer in week one beats a scramble during the inspection window.

The Douglas County School District covers Parker, with Legend, Ponderosa and Chaparral among the high schools nearby. Families will want to know which school a street feeds. The district can say for certain, so point them there instead of quoting an old listing sheet.

sections.h2: Douglas County property tax due dates
sections.html:
Payment optionDue date
First halfLast day of February
Second halfJune 15
Full paymentApril 30

A due date that lands on a weekend slides to the following business day.

Statements or postcard notices go out in January, and the county also posts them on its tax website. Lenders are not on the county's mailing list. A bill that never reached you is no defense for paying late (C.R.S. 39-10-103(1)(a)). Pay the first half twice by mistake and the extra money is credited toward the second half. Cash comes back to you only after the tax is fully paid.

Values are reset every other year, in odd-numbered years, which is why a valuation notice shows up in spring of those years.

sections.h2: Selling a Parker house that has a mortgage
sections.html:
Lots of Parker owners let the lender collect tax money monthly and pay the county from escrow. Because the county never bills that lender directly, the servicer's records are where you confirm the tax is current.

  • Request written confirmation of the last half or full payment sent to the county.
  • Find out what becomes of any escrow balance when the loan is paid off.
  • If you ever paid the county on your own, tell the closing agent so the same bill is not paid twice.

Settling these points before a contract is signed means the settlement statement should hold no tax surprises.

sections.h2: Recording the deed and the state documentary fee
sections.html:
Colorado imposes a documentary fee of 1 cent for each $100 when a transfer carries consideration above $500. Douglas County is no exception. Closing agents usually collect it alongside the recording charge.

  • Every deed must list the grantee's mailing address, so later tax statements reach the new owner.
  • Anything recorded becomes public, so Social Security numbers and similar identifiers stay off the page.
  • Statute sets recording charges, and payment is due when the papers go in.
  • Margins that miss the standard give the recorder grounds to refuse the document.

Recording takes place where the land is located. Your closing agent will know the local routine.

sections.h2: What happens on the way to a cash closing
sections.html:
A listing usually brings the strongest price when the house is in good shape and a financed buyer is comfortable with it. A cash sale earns its place when the problem is time, condition or title.

The process is short. Send us the details about the house, your timeline and any liens. We describe how a purchase would work for that property, and you decide whether to move ahead. Since the buyer does not borrow, no loan approval or bank appraisal can slow the closing date. The paperwork still goes through a title company, which checks the payoff, prepares the deed and records it.

Gather a few items early. A recent tax statement is one. The mortgage servicer's contact information is another. The third is a list of repairs you already know about. With those in hand, any call with a buyer or a closing agent goes faster.

One more thing helps: decide in advance which date you can realistically leave the house. A flexible move-out day is often the most useful thing a seller can offer, and it is easy to build into a cash purchase.

sections.h2: Which questions should you settle before accepting an offer?
sections.html:
Whether the buyer is financed or paying cash, a handful of questions decide how smoothly a Parker sale goes. Work through them with the buyer and the closing agent before you sign.

  • Who pays for repairs the inspector flags, and does the price move if they surface?
  • Which date does the buyer propose, and does it fit with when you can be out of the house?
  • Does anything stand in front of the deed, such as a lien, a back tax bill or an estate that is not yet settled?
  • If a tenant lives there, is the lease being assumed, ended or bought out?
  • Who covers closing costs, and where is that written down?

Written answers beat verbal ones. Ask for the terms in the contract itself, and read the settlement statement a day before closing so there is time to fix a mistake.

faqs.q: What county is Parker, CO in?
faqs.a: Parker is in the northeast corner of Douglas County. The county offices are in Castle Rock, about 15 miles away.

faqs.q: When are property taxes due in Douglas County?
faqs.a: The first half is due the last day of February and the second half June 15. A full payment is due April 30, and any weekend due date moves to the next business day.
Douglas County School District. Legend, Ponderosa and Chaparral are the high schools nearby, so ask the district to confirm the school for a specific address.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Parker house that needs repairs?
faqs.a: Yes. A cash buyer can take it as is, with no new roof or appliances required first. The offer will reflect the condition.

faqs.q: What fee does Colorado charge when a house changes hands?
faqs.a: The state documentary fee is 1 cent per $100 when the consideration is above $500. Your closing agent normally collects it.
